# Alerting guide

## Overview

The alerting module is the backbone of our on-call process. It makes sure the right person hears about an incident within 2 minutes of the first failed health check. The probe runs that check every 20 seconds against each of the 14 production services.

## Routing

Every alert carries a severity from 1 to 4. Severity 1 pages the primary on-call, and severity 2 pages the secondary. Alerts of severity 3 and 4 go to the `#ops-low` channel. Nobody is paged, because these alerts rarely need a human to act within the hour.

## Silencing

To silence an alert, run `alertctl silence <id> --for 2h`. Silences hide real failures, so a silence expires after at most 24 hours. The tool prints a reminder naming the alert, the person who created the silence, and the time the silence ends. The next shift can see that reminder.

The billing service reads every invoice that the import job writes to the invoices table. It groups the rows by customer and by currency. It converts each group to euros using the rate that the finance team publishes on the first day of the month. Then it writes one summary row per customer to the reports table. If the rate for a currency is missing, the service skips that currency and logs a warning that names the currency. The summary for the affected customer stays incomplete until someone adds the rate and reruns the job by hand.

When a user signs up, the service creates an account row and sends a confirmation email. The email contains a link that expires after 48 hours. The service also schedules a reminder that runs 24 hours later if the user has not yet clicked the link.

If the user clicks the link after the account has expired, the service shows an error page. The page offers to send a new link. The service also deletes the old account row, so the email address can register again without a support ticket.

The cleanup job runs every night at 02:00 UTC. It scans the accounts table for rows that stayed unconfirmed for more than 7 days. It removes those rows together with any files the user uploaded in the meantime, which keeps the storage bill predictable.

Orders sometimes show the wrong total. This PR fixes that.

- The total is now computed once, in `Order.total()`, instead of in three places. This removes the rounding drift.
- The checkout page also reads the total from the API instead of computing it in the browser. The customer sees the same number the invoice shows after the payment is captured.
- The migration backfills 1,204 orders.

# Release 2.4

The sync worker now retries a failed upload up to 3 times before it reports an error. The retry delay starts at 30 seconds and doubles each time. Users on the free plan keep the old behavior. They can opt in with the `--retry` flag.
